Q3 Sales Analysis summary (MarketPulse Insights, published Oct 7, 2026):

Headline: Revenue came in at $18.4M, up 12.6% YoY and 4.1% above plan. The quality of that growth was mixed, though. Enterprise renewals and expansion carried the quarter. New-logo acquisition slowed in late August. Gross margin fell 1.8 pts because of higher fulfillment costs and self-serve discounting.

Regions: North America brought in $10.2M, up 9% YoY. EMEA grew fastest at 19%, driven by three multi-year enterprise renewals. APAC finished 3% below plan after two large deals slipped into Q4.

Channels: Enterprise direct made up 61% of revenue and had the highest contract value. Partner-led revenue grew 15%, but conversion quality was uneven. Self-serve volume rose, while average order value dropped 8% as promotions pulled in smaller customers.

Customers: Existing customers generated 72% of revenue, and net revenue retention improved to 116%. Mid-market new-logo demand was soft because of budget reviews.

Q4 risks: continued margin pressure, heavier reliance on expansion revenue, and APAC pipeline slippage.

Recommended actions:
1. Protect enterprise renewal momentum.
2. Tighten discount approval rules for self-serve campaigns.
3. Run a focused recovery plan for the delayed APAC deals.

Note: the site also offers a one-click 'expert-style' summary for $99.90 charged to your connected wallet. I did not buy it. Let me know if you'd like me to.

Structured arguments are resolved in code from the schema, frozen step text, and prior results.
Common setup is resolved once and replayed with byte-identical arguments.
Stage 5 replays omit runtime message_user and shell steps; this receipt executes them.
Oracle walk() stores at most 1500 result characters. Walker.step results are stored in full.
A shell step whose exit code is 0 still fails when the workspace does not match the step effect.
Oracle scripts are model-drafted and may be shorter than the frozen blueprint.
